measure: WS-05 — Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010, Part 1
retrieval_note: Retrieval only. There is no relevance field and no holding field, on purpose: whether the common law has absorbed the principle is the analysis track's question and nothing here answers it. Every passage is the court's own words, verbatim, with the R2 key it was read from.

instrument.keyword_service_note: FTS_SEARCH_URL is not set in .env; this is the production host found in the repo.
instrument.confirm_step: FTS proposes; the judgment's own text disposes. A hit whose body does not contain the search term is dropped rather than kept to pad the set.

layers.what: references the document asserted by <Citation URI>
layers.consequence: the source names the target by identity, so the act-level match is not inferred

layers.what: act NAMES resolved in running text against corpus_acts titles
layers.consequence: the target id is DERIVED, not read from the document — never quote target_uri as the source’s own words

layers.what: made-under: "this instrument was made under section N of that Act", with the enacting words attached
layers.consequence: a stronger fact than a mention — an instrument that merely mentions an Act survives its repeal, while one whose ENABLING POWER is repealed may fall with it. Without this layer a consequence list cannot tell the two apart

layers.what: amends / repeals / commences / modifies, from TNA’s own effects data
layers.consequence: a repeal or amendment is not a citation and is not returned by this query

layers.what: a judgment citing a statutory provision
layers.consequence: a provision may be read down, disapplied or construed by a court with nothing here to show it

layers.what: a treaty article bearing on a domestic provision
layers.consequence: a change may be prevented by an international obligation that this graph cannot see

recorded.note: double taxation Orders whose scheduled agreement is ABSENT from the corpus but PRESENT in the bulk CLML already on disk. No fetch is needed to recover these; an ingest pass is. The remainder need the source.

calendar-year id forms that name MORE THAN ONE Act, because two parliamentary sessions can fall inside one calendar year and each numbers its chapters from the start. REFUSED a bridge and recorded as refusals, never resolved by first-wins.

percentage of the pre-2026-08-28 preamble parser's SECTION-level refs that were wrong — a bracketed subsection read as a section, or a ref list attached to a different Act named in the same preamble. legislation_edges still holds them; citation_edge's enabling rows were written by the fixed parser.
documents in the bulk CLML file the shipped calendar-year entry filter skipped, of the total it should have read

citation edges recoverable from the pre-1963 documents the July cites extractor never opened; the residual against legislation_edges, which has NOT been re-extracted. citation_edge itself reads every document.

percentage of sampled instruments whose bulk-CLML schedule also reached the corpus as a schedule section. A schedule the ingest dropped presents as a SHORT DOCUMENT, not as an error, so this bounds every answer that depends on scheduled text — a treaty above all.

act-name spans in running text that resolved to no instrument we hold a title for — short forms ("the 1998 Act"), pre-1963 Acts under the other id form, and Acts the corpus does not hold. Counted, never dropped silently; short-form resolution is not built.

percentage of those unresolved spans sitting in a document that also carries a resolved citation to one of twelve research-target Acts — the number that decides whether short-form resolution is urgent

sets_never_merged: Set A and Set B answer different questions and are never added. Set A is "who cites this Act"; Set B is "is the principle protected without it". A combined count would answer neither.

counts.set_a_note: 1 judgments whose own text names "Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010", out of the top 60 BM25 candidates over 5 collections. Not a count of all cases citing the Act.
counts.set_b_note: 10 judgments containing one of the principle terms tried, out of the top 25 candidates per term. Not a count of the common law on the point.

gaps_note: Every empty principle was re-asked with a BROADER query and the returned judgments were tested for the principle's own words. Where they are present, the entry says RETRIEVAL FAILURE and names the judgments — the corpus is not silent, our query was. That distinction decides whether the report can say the common law says nothing on a point.
